cases.title: Review a change without making it live
cases.summary: Separate the currently accepted version from proposals that are ready for review or promotion.

inputFiles.description: Accepted package, version, assertion, evidence, decision, and promotion baseline.
Review-ready, decision-ready, promotion-ready, and blocked proposal states.

questions.question: Which version is currently accepted?
questions.answerSummary: Version 1 remains the accepted state because it is the target of the latest promotion record.
questions.whyItMatters: A mutable label cannot silently replace the decision and promotion lineage that establishes current state.

caveats: current state is derived from the latest promotion record, not mutable package truth
active package version must match the latest promotion target

questions.question: Is Proposal B already current because it was approved?
questions.answerSummary: No. Proposal B is promotion-ready, but it has no promotion record and Version 1 remains current.
questions.whyItMatters: Approval and promotion remain different events, preventing proposed state from masquerading as accepted reality.

cases.title: Trace a claim to its evidence
cases.summary: Follow an accepted assertion through its source artifact, evidence, validation, governance, promotion, and version history.

inputFiles.description: Accepted assertion with source, artifact, evidence, validation, review, decision, promotion, and version lineage.

questions.question: Where did the accepted claim come from?
questions.answerSummary: The claim came from the vendor-page artifact, which retains its source and extracted evidence references.
questions.whyItMatters: A reader can inspect the source carrier instead of trusting an ungrounded answer.

questions.question: What governance lineage made this evidence part of accepted state?
questions.answerSummary: The evidence is linked through validation, review, an approving decision, promotion, and the accepted version history.
questions.whyItMatters: Evidence presence is kept separate from the governance events that make a version current.

questions.question: Can the accepted assertion be traced all the way back to its source?
questions.answerSummary: Yes. The assertion exposes its evidence, artifact, source, validation, review, decision, promotion, and version references.
questions.whyItMatters: The answer remains auditable from canonical assertion back to the external source identity.

boundaryNote: Reference-case answers are deterministic read-model proof. They do not create evidence, canonical truth, review approval, governance decisions, promotion, certification, release authority, or backend equivalence.
